fields.label: Element GUID
fields.description: The IFC GlobalId, exactly as it appears in the IFC file. This is the join key Phase 3's viewer uses to turn a picked element back into a model entity, so it must be the file's own value and never a re-encoded or re-derived one.

fields.label: Element Type
fields.description: IFC entity name, e.g. IFCWALL. Recorded so a lookup failure can say what was being looked for without re-reading the IFC.

fields.label: IFC Step Id
fields.description: The `#N` instance number from the IFC DATA section, so a row can be traced back to the exact line it came from.

fields.label: Drawing
fields.description: The sheet or drawing this element appears on. Part of the Element<->Drawing Map the split view's Sync Selection reads.

fields.label: Drawing Page
fields.description: 1-based page within the drawing, for multi-page PDFs.

fields.label: Drawing Region
fields.description: The element's bounding region on that page, in PDF user units. This is the edge the 2D viewport highlights, so it is stored rather than derived: the mapping is a DECISION made once, and recomputing it from a sheet nobody has calibrated would move the highlight every time the scale changed.

fields.label: Mapped Area
fields.description: The area measured ON THE SHEET, in m2, for this region. This is the PDF side of the comparison. Deliberately NOT 'area': nothing in this app measures a per-element IFC area, and a field by that name would be read as one that does.

fields.label: Geometry Surface Area (m2)
fields.description: Renamed from `surface_area`. The child table now carries THREE quantities that all read as 'area' -- `mapped_area` (the BOQ/quantity the coordinator typed against this element), `geom_surface_area` (true mesh surface, the sum of triangle areas) and `geom_footprint_area` (the XY bounding box). They are not interchangeable: for a 200x3000x200 wall the surface is ~2.5 m2 and the footprint ~0.06 m2. A QS reading `surface_area` next to `mapped_area` has no way to tell which is which, which is how a takeoff gets silently misread -- so the geometry-derived pair is prefixed.
